moat_against: Price-transparent commodity seat product — fare premium re-won daily vs Delta, American, ULCCs
Economics leak to inputs — union labor captures gains each contract cycle; unhedged fuel (Q2 2026 fuel +84% YoY erased a +16% revenue quarter's profit growth)
Poor through-cycle returns — OE negative in 2 of the last 5 years; net debt 6.36x normalized OE
Regulators, not United, set the capacity ceilings binding at Newark and O'Hare
moat_for: Irreplicable fortress hubs (Newark, San Francisco, Denver, Houston, O'Hare) with slot/gate constraints; largest U.S. carrier on Atlantic and Pacific
MileagePlus loyalty economy — high-margin, cash-up-front co-brand sales; loyalty revenue +11% in Q2 2026
Scale and premium mix — largest mainline fleet, upgauging lowers unit cost; premium revenue +16.4% in Q2 2026
Star Alliance feed and corporate contracts filling the international network
moat_justification: Irreplicable hub geography (Newark, San Francisco, Denver, Houston, O'Hare fortresses; largest U.S. carrier across Atlantic and Pacific), MileagePlus loyalty economics with cash-up-front co-brand sales, scale/upgauging unit-cost advantage and a premium mix compounding at double digits — against a price-transparent commodity seat product, union labor and fuel capturing the economics each cycle, negative OE in 2 of the last 5 years, and 6.4x net debt / normalized OE.
name: United Airlines Holdings, Inc.
one_liner: Best-network U.S. airline, moat 4/10 — executing well (record revenue, premium/loyalty compounding, guidance raised into a fuel shock), but on normalized SBC-adjusted owner's earnings of $7.33/share the $103.50 price yields only a 10.1% weighted IRR (IV@15% $62.38) because cyclical OE levered 6.4x must carry a heavy fleet-capex cycle; it clears 15% only at ~$62.
